correctness.rationale: Strict endomorphisms of loopless C_n for even n have +/-1 cyclic steps with winding ±n (2n automorphisms) or zero (n*binomial(n,n/2) bridge maps). For bridge span h, regularity is equivalent to a cyclic full monotone run of length h. Marking each such run and filling the complement by a strip-constrained path gives T_n=2n²Σ_h W_{n,h} and I_n=1+nΣ W_{n,h}. Distinct full runs cannot overlap, so pairs of runs are bounded by P_n≤2n³Σ_h[2cos(π/(h+2))]^(n-2h); the excess over unique runs is at most P_n. Uniform strip eigenvalue bounds and a positive pair of leading endpoint eigenprojections give log Σ_hW=n log2-K n^(1/3)+O(log n) where K=3π^(2/3)(log2)^(2/3)/2. The second-run exponent is 2^(2/3)K, hence R_n/(2nI_n)→1 with relative error exp[-δ n^(1/3)] for every δ<(2^(2/3)-1)K. Direct exact semigroup enumeration at n=4,6,8 and independent step-word counts beyond corroborate finite identities, not the uniform asymptotic.

value.rationale: A natural semigroup statistic—the density of von Neumann regular transformations relative to idempotents—is sharply evaluated for an infinite graph family. The asymptotic factor 2n and explicit stretched-exponential suppression of extra full runs reveal an interpretable structural law beyond a known regularity decision criterion. A future semigroup enumeration or random-walk asymptotics study could use this unique-witness result.
